title: The History of AI Coding Tools: From Autocomplete to Agents (2026)
summary: The complete history of AI coding tools, from 1996 autocomplete to 2026 agent fleets. Verified dates, benchmark scores, and every generation explained.
body_text: A subagent is a helper spawned by a main agent, with its own context window and a narrow job like searching a codebase or reviewing a diff. Only its conclusion returns. This keeps thousands of tokens of intermediate output out of the main conversation, which is one of the main reasons 2026 agents run for hours where 2024 agents ran for minutes. See subagents and context compaction . Thirty years of this history point in one direction: the machine keeps taking the next layer of typing, and the human keeps moving up to the next layer of judgement. IntelliSense took the identifier. Copilot took the function. Agents took the pull request. What none of them took, and what no roadmap suggests they will, is knowing what should exist in the first place. That is the loop worth building for. Memory of what your team knows, intelligence that decides what to do with it, execution that actually runs. Start with a prompt and see what comes back. ▲ ■ ● Featured image: Univac I Supervisory Control Console (Remington Rand, 1951) at the Computer History Museum. title: NextEra Energy and Dominion Energy file to combine, building a stronger company to meet growing power demand across four of America's fastest-growing states while keeping energy affordable and reliable
summary: NextEra Energy and Dominion Energy file applications seeking regulatory approval of their proposed combination Customers in Virginia, North Carolina and South Carolina would receive $2.25 billion...
body_text: NextEra Energy and Dominion Energy file applications seeking regulatory approval of their proposed combination Customers in Virginia, North Carolina and South Carolina would receive $2.25 billion in shareholder-funded bill credits, and the companies have committed that merger-related costs will not be passed on to customers The combination brings together Dominion Energy's local leadership, experienced workforce and community knowledge with NextEra Energy's added financial strength, supply chain expertise and infrastructure development capabilities The combined company would bring an all-of-the-above energy platform, including renewables, battery storage, nuclear and natural gas, with industry-leading capabilities Dominion Energy's operating companies will remain locally led and separately regulated, with meaningful job protections; the combined company would maintain dual corporate headquarters in Richmond, Virginia, and Juno Beach, Florida, and an operational headquarters in Cayce, South Carolina The combination positions Virginia, North Carolina and South Carolina to meet unprecedented power demand, support jobs and economic development, and keep customer bills affordable The transaction is expected to close in the second half of 2027 JUNO BEACH, Fla. and RICHMOND, Va. , July 15, 2026 / PRNewswire / -- NextEra Energy, Inc. (NYSE: NEE) and Dominion Energy, Inc. (NYSE: D) today filed applications seeking regulatory approval of their proposed combination with the Virginia State Corporation Commission, the North Carolina Utilities Commission, the Public Service Commission of South Carolina, the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission and the Nuclear Regulatory Commission. America is entering an era of rapidly growing electricity demand that will require substantial investment in generation, transmission, distribution and grid resilience. The proposed combination is designed to preserve Dominion Energy's local strengths with NextEra Energy's added resources, balance sheet strength, supply chain expertise, construction experience and operating capabilities to help meet that demand reliably and affordably over the long term. The combined company would serve approximately 10 million customer accounts across four of the nation's fastest-growing states and be better positioned to buy, build, finance and operate the energy infrastructure customers need more efficiently. The larger platform is intended to complement, not replace, Dominion Energy's local operating model. Dominion Energy's operating companies would remain locally led, separately regulated and accountable to their state commissions, while their teams gain access to additional technology, capital and proven practices. That includes a proven track record at Florida Power & Light Company (FPL) with more than 20 years of reliably and affordably meeting growth in one of the fastest-growing states in America, with a reliability performance of more than 60% better than the national average and a typical residential bill approximately 30% below the national average. A word from John Ketchum, chairman, president and CEO of NextEra Energy: "This combination is about putting scale and a stronger, more comprehensive platform behind Dominion Energy's local teams so they can meet growing power demand while keeping bills affordable and service reliable. We're bringing together two industry-leading teams with complementary strengths and expertise. Dominion Energy brings deep local knowledge, experienced employees and a strong operating record. NextEra Energy brings additional scale, an industry-leading operating platform, financial strength, supply chain expertise and operating efficiencies we have built through FPL and NextEra Energy Resources. Together, we will be better positioned to partner with states and communities to attract new investment, support new jobs and invest in the all-of-the-above energy infrastructure customers need, including renewables, battery storage, nuclear and gas-fired generation. Customers would experience immediate value through $2.25 billion in shareholder-funded bill credits and long-term value through a stronger company that can buy, build, finance and operate energy infrastructure projects more efficiently, which will result in long-term customer benefits." A word from Robert Blue, chair, president and CEO of Dominion Energy: "This is a combination centered on customers, communities and employees. It preserves the Dominion Energy utilities our customers know — the same local leaders, employees, regulatory oversight and commitment to an all-of-the-above energy mix — while adding capabilities that can help us build needed infrastructure more efficiently and keep bills affordable. Our employees and communities can be confident that we will remain a strong local employer, a constructive economic development partner and a reliable provider of the energy that powers homes, businesses and new investments." Delivering real value to customers, communities and employees Immediate bill relief and customer protections: Dominion Energy customers in Virginia, North Carolina and South Carolina would receive $2.25 billion in bill credits over the first two years after closing, funded by shareholders and not recoverable from customers. Customers also would be held harmless from any and all transaction, transition, acquisition-premium, financing and restructuring costs associated with the combination. Long-term affordability and reliability: The benefits extend beyond the initial credits. The combined company's greater purchasing power, broader supply chain visibility, increased access to capital, project execution capabilities and larger operating platform are expected to help meet growing power demand affordably while maintaining service quality and reliability. An all-of-the-above energy platform: Through its regulated utilities and subsidiaries, the combined company would own or operate more than 110 gigawatts of electric generating resources across renewables, battery storage, nuclear and natural gas. The combination would pair Dominion Energy's local operating expertise and generation portfolio with NextEra Energy's industry-leading solar and battery storage capabilities, as well as deep experience in nuclear, natural gas, transmission and grid modernization. Customer service and storm response: The combination would provide access to a larger regulated utility platform, drawing on best practices across FPL and Dominion Energy's operating companies in customer service, storm restoration, grid modernization, workforce tools, data analytics, artificial intelligence and process improvement. Locally led, locally staffed and fully accountable: Dominion Energy's operating companies will remain separately regulated and locally led. The combined company will maintain dual corporate headquarters in Richmond, Virginia, and Juno Beach, Florida, and an operational headquarters in Cayce, South Carolina. State regulators would continue to oversee rates, service, resource planning and major investments. Dominion Energy employees would receive 18 months of job protection after closing; non-union employees would receive two years of current compensation and comparable benefits. Collective bargaining agreements would continue according to their terms. A partner in economic and community development: Reliable, affordable energy is foundational to economic development. The combined company intends to partner with state and local leaders to support existing employers, attract new businesses, and encourage additional investment from suppliers, contractors and service providers. It also would increase Dominion Energy's historical shareholder-funded charitable giving by $10 million annually for five years across Virginia, North Carolina and South Carolina. Transaction review process The transaction has been unanimously approved by the boards of directors of both companies. The transaction is expected to close in the second half of 2027, subject to customary closing conditions and approvals by the shareholders of NextEra Energy and Dominion Energy, state regulatory review and approval from the Virginia State Corporation Commission, the North Carolina Utilities Commission and the Public Service Commission of South Carolina, the expiration or termination of the waiting period under the Hart-Scott-Rodino Antitrust Improvements Act, approval by the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission under Section 203 of the Federal Power Act and approval by the Nuclear Regulatory Commission. More information about the proposed combination is available at www.DominionNextEraFuture.com . Applications will be posted as they are filed. About NextEra Energy, Inc. NextEra Energy, Inc. (NYSE: NEE) is the largest electric power and energy infrastructure company in North America, the world's leader in renewables and storage and a leading provider of electricity to American homes and businesses. Headquartered in Juno Beach, Florida, NextEra Energy is a Fortune 200 company that owns Florida Power & Light Company, America's largest electric utility, which provides reliable electricity to approximately 12 million people across Florida. NextEra Energy also owns the largest energy infrastructure development company in the U.S., NextEra Energy Resources, LLC. NextEra Energy and its affiliated entities are meeting America's growing energy needs with a diverse mix of energy sources, including renewables, battery storage, nuclear and natural gas. For more information about NextEra Energy companies, visit these websites: www.NextEraEnergy.com, www.FPL.com , www.NextEraEnergyResources.com . About Dominion Energy Dominion Energy (NYSE: D), headquartered in Richmond, Va., provides regulated electricity service to 3.6 million homes and businesses in Virginia, North Carolina and South Carolina, and regulated natural gas service to 500,000 customers in South Carolina. The company is one of the nation's leading developers and operators of regulated offshore wind and solar power and the largest producer of carbon-free electricity in New England. The company's mission is to provide the reliable, affordable and increasingly clean energy that powers its customers every day. Please visit DominionEnergy.com to learn more. title: Chaos Conductors: Turning Market Disruption into Your Competitive Symphony
summary: Disruption is constant – and marketing leaders are expected to lead with resilience, clarity, and confidence.
body_text: On-Demand Webinar | 36:46 Chaos Conductors: Turning Market Disruption into Your Competitive Symphony Hear how top marketing leaders turn chaos into clarity and disruption into strategy. Disruption is constant – and marketing leaders are expected to lead with resilience, clarity, and confidence. In this session, David Edelman, Executive Advisor Harvard Business School, former CMO at Aetna, and Polly Nicholas, CXO at Unum, share real-world strategies they’ve used to guide teams through transformation, implement AI that works, and make confident decisions amid uncertainty. You’ll leave with practical frameworks to manage change, align stakeholders, and turn chaos into strategy. Why watch Discover practical frameworks for integrating AI without falling into the hype trap. Get actionable insights to transform constant change into momentum. Explore leadership tactics that help teams stay focused and energized through transformation. Learn how to make confident decisions – even when you are still gathering the data. Welcome everybody. I'm Dave Edelman and I'm here with the third in our webinar series Inside the Mind of the Modern CMO and this is sponsored by Pega, who has been leading the way in personalization capabilities for decades, an area that I personally have been very close to. I am absolutely thrilled to be here with Polly Nicholas, the Chief Experience Officer of Unum and a real true leader in where customer experience, strategy, execution and leadership is going. Thanks, Dave. Great to be here today. What a wonderful opportunity. Yes, it is. And I think we're going to have a great discussion because there's a lot going on in the world around us, but very specifically in the world that you are leading at Unum. So Polly, you are the first Chief Experience Officer at Unum and you're leading a transformation of a company from a more product focus to a more solutions oriented approach to delivering value. Could you share with us some more about the journey that Unum is on and why does that require the leadership of a new capability such as a CXO? Well, Dave, before we get started today, I just I want to mention what an incredible leader you are in this space. You know, love about your intersection of a couple of key things are one, how you bridge thought leadership, real world execution and shaping the way we think about how marketing and CX should come together. As we look to have this great conversation today. I just, I appreciate the opportunity to listen and learn from you as well as the chance to share. You know what we're up to at Unum. Well, thank you, Polly. That's very, very nice. And it certainly is mutual. I learned a ton from our conversations as well. And I'm sure I will from this. As we, you know, you asked the question about what it feels like to be the first CXO at Unum in the journey that we're on. A lot of people don't know, you know, they don't know, you know, by name. We touch over 38 million lives and when you think about the peoples and families we interact with, we're really there. You know, sometimes in the toughest moments, we're there when somebody has a medical leave, a disability claim, often a moment of uncertainty. So I do think, you know, it's really interesting to lead and be a part of such an incredible organization that has such a big impact. And when you asked about, you know, the why, you know what, why are we transforming? That is why we're transforming. So it's not just the offer of the benefits we provide to employees, it's how we deliver it. No, getting money into someone's account within 24 hours from a claims approval date with tools like Zell isn't just about innovation. It's about making sure that, you know, is the easiest part of someone's hardest moment. And so it's been really an opportunity for me and for the broader Unum organization is to really reimagine how we can continue to show up and be that, be that provider, you know, you know, we think about being the easiest part of what might be a difficult moment. And it isn't just about what we do. It's who we are as an organization and are there things in the external environment Poly that are shaping where you're going? Is there is this internally driven from Unum? Are you seeing it because it's a way that you've got to compete and raise the bar? Are there also things happening in the environment that are leading you to be even more CX solutions oriented? Absolutely, Dave. You know one of the things that is especially moving fast in our involving market is leave laws and employee expectations. We're fortunate that we have increased our company understanding and acumen around both of these topics in both the topics of leave and technology. Fortunately, we've been in the lead business for over 25 years. So we have a lot of embedded expertise and we've invested quite a lot over the last few years in transforming this experience of taking time away from work. And so in an example, I just, you know, as you think about being a listener about how that turns into value, our government affairs team spends quite a bit of time out influencing both federal and state laws as it relates to leave. And then we bring that back to our existing employers, the people that are our customers. Interestingly enough, we recently had a lead webinar series where we talked about how we can help and enable employers navigate the lead landscape. We had over 22,000 of our current customers signed up for that. Your theories and you know why that's important? Well, it means that we're answering the questions that are being asked by the customers we serve. And that's really where we see incredible value for us as an organization and more importantly, test our purpose. The complexity sounds staggering from an employer's point of view with all the different laws at a federal and state level that different kinds of leave that are available now that people are taking, probably also just the amount of leave taking, people taking advantage of, of benefits. So from an employer's perspective, juggling that all themselves, even if you were just the insurance provider still had put a lot of onus on them to manage it. So now you're saying we have to be able to provide a whole outsource solution for managing leave so that we can dramatically simplify what the employer has to deal with and also, in the end, make it easier for the covered employee. Is that the right way of thinking about it? That's exactly it. Yep. And so as you do that, you've got brokers through whom you sell and get connected with employers. You've got the employers who we just talked about, you've got the covered employees. Just from Unum's perspective, that's a whole lot of complexity. And if you're in charge of customer experience, those are three completely different customers, stakeholders to manage. How do you think about your prioritization and managing the differences? Do you have different groups focused on different constituencies? Do you have certain priorities and sequencing? How do you manage in that complexity? It's a great question, Dave. And you are right, we essentially have three key customers. We have our broker, we have employers and we have employee brokers want the competence that are offering is going to deliver client satisfaction to their constituents, their employers, the employers they help every day. So we think a lot about enabling brokers to understand our end and offering through the eyes of that employer. Let me describe then how we think about employers. You know you use the word simplification. The reality is that the HR function, the payroll function, the HR technology function inside organizations have a lot of things coming their way and a lot of demands. Simplification is everything for that employer. Making it easy to consume information and take that logical next step is critical. And so for employers, it's simplification. But at the end of the day, if we treat employees well, if we help that claimant in their time of need, if we're there making that hard moment the easiest thing we possibly can, then we delivered for all the constituents that are part of our ecosystem. So we really do think about all three. For brokers, we again want the right experience for them and we want to keep their clients happy. Which are those employers? For employers, they need simplification. They need clear, direct action to understand what their very next step is. And then finally, employees need empathy, they need compassion. They need somebody on the other end of the phone and or on that chat to help them and or for information they can get 24/7 as they need it digitally. And as you're doing this, Polly, it, it feels like this is not just a natural extension. This is a a transformation of how people have likely thought about the business, even thinking about brokers. Most of the way you were selling before was an insurance product, disability insurance, leave protection. And now you're creating a broader solution. So a heck of a lot more surface area in which you're interacting with people. So this is, I think one of the things that you're stepping into this breach to say we've got to change people's minds externally and even internally. We now have to take on the responsibility for doing so much more. Is that the way you've seen your role? And how do you think Then also in terms of the mindset shift externally and internally, how are you working that? Yeah, Dave, it's a great question. And it is about transforming marketplaces, it's about transforming inside Unum and it's about transforming on behalf of our customers. And so that is both the challenge and the opportunity to deliver excellence, to deliver excellence proactively across key customer touch points. Let me make that concrete. As you think about that employer for our largest segment, we recognize that there isn't just one person on the other side of our experience who sits on the employer site. There's somebody from payroll or somebody from the HR technology team. There's a leave expert or a leave admin individual. There's that frontline manager who's just trying to ensure, let's say on a store that other people show up. So they you work every single day. And so one of the efforts that we really had underway that's been illuminating for our organization is to understand those different HR personas and to truly think about how are the data and insights we're providing them, helping them take what I would describe as their next best action. So by way of an example, if you're a frontline manager at a pizza shop, what you want to do is have your people there to make pizza. You don't really care about anything else. And unlocking neck level value by understanding those HR personas means that we can truly help that employer simplify the things they need, understand how to take their next best action, and ensure that ultimately they're being able to deliver for their broader business objectives, which is really what we want to get after. How do we get that next person return to work in a way that they're excited to be back and ensure that the business understands how to manage Bob Airway? So wow, there's a lot there that you're starting to get into now in terms of data, technology, next best action, things that drive much more personalized experiences. Let's dig into that a bit more, Polly. I mean, after all, we're on a webinar from Pega, so we might as well just probe a bit on how you're thinking about technology. Are you taking the technology you have and just trying to figure out how far can we push it? All of the above. How do you think about the interactions with your tech team? Because they have to be a crucial partner for you. But you're the Chief experience officer, Dave. I would tie back to even higher up our corporate strategy and then thinking about how that corporate strategy comes through and delivers for our customers. So let me start with one. Our purpose is what guides us helping to work in the world drives throughout life's moments. That truly is why we show up every day and that is a customer centric mindset. Definitely understand what your durable business strategy is. We have a really good framework we use at Unum that guides us as we think about our strategic. You can't be focused on everything. So defining what your strategic capabilities are and where you're going to be a difference maker in the marketplace and how that delivers competitive advantage is critical. And then finally, you know, if you think about sort of the three things that it takes to build a good durable organization, understand the financial objectives of your organization. So understand how you deliver customer experience, but how you're going to measure that for your financial outcomes for the organization. And so when you ask the question a little bit about how do you work with your tech teams or is it tech LED or is it business LED, the answer is it must be purpose and strategy LED. We must start with customers at the center. And a couple of the ways we're doing this are one, we're bringing together the end to end functions across the organization to solve problems. A recent example of that within Unum was that we were launching a brand new capability 1125 and it was an important capability in the marketplace because it connected many of our products together in the eyes of the customer. It was bringing our supplemental health benefits which help support somebody when they often have a key accident or hospitalization whether other elite. So great to bring that together. But what we did was we brought together an end to end team. Think about the contact center folks, the folks that process claim, the individuals that built the technology, the sales team, the marketing team, really that end to end team. And we interrogated a set of pilot customers. You understand was the experience we described actually and what we had, what we uncovered was there was a lot of things that were going really well and what we imagined to be true was in fact mostly true. But we also found some places where we could do it better. And by bringing that cross functional team together, by seeing marketing and CX as the description of the experience we were delivering and the actual experience we were delivering, we got to a better set of key priority. Some that happened in the room, some that happened 1125 or soon after and some that are even still happening about how we could improve that customer experience. And I don't think until you really bring that holistic organizational view together in the eyes of the customer, do you see where there is what you would describe as surface area to get after to solve for customer needs. And when you did that and brought everybody together, that could be a lot of people. How are you? Are you guiding the whole discussion through a vision of what you expect the customer experience to be? That's the foundation of where you want it to go. And then you're starting to see what's actually happening, what's possible, where the breakpoints. Is that how you guide that conversation? Because it could be a lot of people in a room. You know, not only did we guide what we hoped and expect for the customer, we actually came forward with one. What is that customer going through? So we provided throughout the day that we were together, we provided a number of examples, verbatims, real life recordings of what it felt like to be a customer. You know, so as we were going through the experience and understanding and interrogating it, not only did we have voice to the customer all the way through our value stream up, we also had live experience, if you will, that people could touch and feel. So as you just define where you want to go and the vision for the future, you also need practical, tactical examples of how it's coming for life today. And what was interesting about that is, you know, one of the wonderful things about Unum is that we have Hogs who have spent most of their career here and they have played roles across the organization. So they come with a wealth of knowledge of the different experiences we create, but there probably wasn't a person that walked out of that room that didn't learn something pretty significant about how we support our customers by spending that time. So it isn't just the moment that we're in, it's also creating a culture that we're going to continue to understand really what that end to end experience looks like and help carry that forward as a steward to future conversations across the organization. And as you do that, one of the things you talked about is having the data also to understand what's going on. Of course, you want the verbatims, you want the customer's point of view, but there's also operational data from your systems that you've got to surface. And it could be that you're asking questions of the data that haven't been asked before. Now when you're looking at it in across functional way, was that a challenge trying to get data to do things that you hadn't really asked it to do before? Data, data, data, right. The data, data, data, data. It drives everything that I think about certainly and, and in the marketing and CF space, it can be the true unlock for an organization. And I'm not unique in that. But what I would say that's interesting about the insurance industry and we are unlike many industries who've been around for a little while is that we've established our experiences historically based on our products, our financial reporting and compliance and legal reasons. So we've created towers of expertise, but not towers of end to end knowledge. And so what's been really, really interesting as you begin to shift your mindset to a product you from a product you to a solution view, you begin to see insights you wouldn't otherwise capture. And what's been fascinating about that is that sparked the next layer of questions for our organization. Examples might be how do you shift from looking at product based satisfaction to end to end customer satisfaction. And when you do look at that, how do you begin to see customer as a whole through the bundle products and offerings we deliver as opposed to the product set? It's a big shift for an organization that grows to Wall Street every day and says we report on our offering based on our voluntary benefits product lines and group benefits lines or Colonial Lifeline. So you can imagine that there are some. Things within our organization that are foundational to how we worked in the past that will need to evolve for the future. One of those things be stayed up and in doing so, I'm assuming you're also talking about a shift in from product columns, let's say of data to actually having databases that can track the customer across products, across channels. I mean, it's a never ending journey. Of course, it's not something you just pull a switch and do, but I assume that's the direction you'd be headed. Not only is it the direction, I get back to being very clear about your stick alignment, where you're focused and how you're going to deliver for customers to drive distinguishable growth that is profitable for the organization is critical. I was recently at an event and they talked a little bit about, you know, as you examine and think about customer experience, one of the things you want to be able to do is prove out that the investments you've made are returning the right value to the customer and to the overall organization. So one of the things that's been critical as a sort of foundational piece as we've set up the CX organization at Unum more broadly is a key partner has been our finance team. Our finance team understands how and where our financials tie back to customers. And so by making that one thing rather than two things, when we think about persistency and CSAT, when we think about the opportunity to understand customer value and lifetime value, the closer we can get that CX function and that finance function together, we get 2 outcomes out of that. One is you build durable models that can be used for a longer period of time for the organization. They really become the centerpiece of informing the organization on where to go both strategically as well as financially. Secondly, you begin to shape the finances to you of what value is to our organization and having them as a partner by your side, I call them friends of finance is never a bad idea when you think about creating a lasting impact to an organization. Yeah, I do have to just in the true confessions. I have to say when I had a similar role in my earlier days at at Aetna, I was very close with the CIO, took a bit too long to get tight with the CFO, had to really catch up on that. And I think that's really important that you have done that, Polly, because the whole perspective of understanding all the levers, whether it's things like reducing calls to the call center, persistence of the actual customer, being able to sell and expand relationships, there's a lot of different levers that come into play. So it's important to get finance in the game and maybe even also to help prioritize which levers you want to go after as you're improving customer experience. Well, that's it, Dave. As you think about that last statement, if we can begin to create a bright view of not only what excellence looks like in the eyes of the customer and again going back to our purpose, we are here to help the working world drive. And it is an incredible opportunity and we have an incredible culture at Unum that really is committed to making that experience come to light. It's wonderful to start at an organization where that's our beginning, but equally as important is being sure that we understand what will drive profitable growth for the organization. And when you begin to pair those two things together, it's not going to happen overnight, but you begin to think about the customer life cycle truly end to end. And that's really what the CXO role has been about. So the moment you experience Unum's brand all the way through renewal, what are those key customer moments? Are we committed yes, to the things we say in our marketing and sales experience? Are they coming to life in the actual realities of our customers? And where we have improvement, how do we drive it to sustain and deliver profitable growth? And as you're thinking about those improvements, Polly, where is AI playing a role? Is that core to it? Is it a key enabler? Is it something that helps in the background in terms of productivity? How are you thinking about that as part of your strategy? Anybody who's doing anything today must be thinking about AIAI is obviously an opportunity and we're focused on leveraging it in very specific ways inside our organization. But I do feel an interesting nugget. I would want a recent session with women and technology theaters that Mackenzie pulls together on an annual basis. That's who cover peers of mine across industry. And one of the key conversations that came out that I thought was illuminating was, you know, how often are your day-to-day people using AI for personal use? Do they understand the opportunity that it delivers? Are your board members using AI for personal use? Do they understand what it can mean for them? And so I think there are sort of two ways that I think about, you know, leveraging AI inside an organization. 1 is how are you encouraging your people day-to-day to use it both in their personal and professional lives in a safe covered way, of course, to understand the unlock that it can deliver for them. And how are you sharing those stories inside your organization, on your team? So that's one of the things we've been really working out within this DFO organization, making it easier and simple, simpler to use AI, ensuring or sharing the stories of the unlock that it delivers. So as we go on this journey, each person has had their own personal positive experience or challenge that they can relate to. So one is start with your people, bring it into your performance friends, think about it as a part of your everyday life inside your organizations. And then at, you know, more broadly, you know, we think about it in a clear way, which is how do you drive the right experience for the customers we serve? An example of where we've used it recently is, you know, somebody calls in and or chats with us on our digital platform. How do we make it simple for our people to access the right information at the right time? There's thousands of pieces of data they might need to get to the review, say I to simplify that process. So the information that individual need is in our hands at the right time in the right way. Another good example of where we've used it at, you know specifically is down, down market. So in our smaller case business, we've begun to use it to understand customer sentiment. Are they satisfied? Are they dissatisfied? Could we begin to understand what risk might be there to lose that customer and how might we take action based on those operational indicators in order to retain that client or what makes a great client and why are they satisfied and how do we get more book like them? So, you know, there's been a number of ways in thinking about AI, but I think it is both run how you help your employees go on that chimney and then two and maybe equally as important, how you build enterprise assets that help the organization more effectively deliver on their objectives. Yeah, there's so many opportunities to constantly learn. One of the things you just said, Polly, I, I want to just zero in on a couple of words you use. You talked about capabilities to solve a business problem that a customer has as opposed to just simply offering capabilities. I think one of the interesting things about moving from products to solutions is that solution solve. They actually solve a problem. That's that's definitionally what a solution should be. Whereas products don't necessarily inherently do that. They should, but they don't necessarily do that. They offer a capability that then somebody might use to to achieve it. And so I find it really interesting now in your world how moving from product to solution at a time when expectations are high, patience is low, your clients are really strapped for time and capabilities are now there to be able to do more, lead you towards that transformation. I mean, when people go into like Chachi BT and ask a question, they, they're looking for a solution that is tailored to them. And I think we're entering something where more and more people have to think about what's the solution we're moving to and how to move towards a solution. Do you get this sense as you were talking with peers and stuff, this transformation that you're in the middle of from products to solutions? Is this something more broadly we're going to inherently see across other companies and other sectors? Is this just a natural consequence of where we're heading now? No, I think it is a natural consequence. I wouldn't say Unum is unique in the thinking, but I would say we're ahead of the curve. You know, as as you described this intersection of technology, of AI and of solutions, the closer you can get to customers, the defining and the value of CXO organization can bring to a company is a really important first. It actually eliminates the fact that what will drive you forward is delivering customer value. And so and how you begin to think about that end to end improvement becomes really, really important. And so you know as as the CXO of Unum grew, one of the things I ensure we do as a part of every key discussion we're having whether we just got out of the by way of example or 262026 funding conversation. And how does that voice shame even the individual scrum teams choices that they're going to make in 2026 as they execute across across that set of priorities? And I'll, I'll describe a little bit about how that comes to life in the leave landscape. One of the things that really matters is that somebody has an end to end solution, everything from leave planning, so they're taking time away to how they return to work. And for an employer, that's what leave administration is. And so one of the questions we'll be continuing to ask our team and ensuring we deliver in the marketplace is are we helping people do everything from Pran to take time away to turn return to work effectively in the eyes of the employer as opposed to the widgets and the individual component pieces that each of the journeys may be thinking about, which are important. How do we serve as a general contractor for the company, bringing in the electrician, bringing in the plumber, bringing in the landscaper to ensure the house looks beautiful, but that all the component pieces tie back to the ultimate vision we have? Well, that's especially true since it involves all these different functions that you are not necessarily directly on top of. You are orchestrating that and so the general contractors, a terrific analogy. I think one other thing you said, which is essentially I think you've answered my last question without realizing it, is that one of the essential capabilities for somebody in your role is the willingness and drive to pound on the table with the customer's point of view to constantly make sure as decisions are being shaped priority said investments made that you've got the richest reality understanding of the customer in mind. And is that, is that fair to say, Polly, that it all starts with that? It does start with that, you know, but David, you think about your experience in marketing and you know, I think the evolution for me that I've observed over the last year and in my role is that if you're in marketing, you're in CX. If you're in CX, you're in marketing because customers want what you sold them upfront, the story you've been telling them to be delivered and that will allow them to 1 be excited about potentially staying with you. 2 is buying that next product that you might be delivering to them. That's a value around. And by continuing to bring that voice of the customer to the, to the conversation inside an organization, you really unlock again, a net new set of value inside the organization. And I was recently having a conversation with a peer of mine and, you know, they had done some work to understand a little bit more about brand and what their brand meant. And in that story, brand meant culture and the customer experience they were creating. It is that simple. And so I think as you think about organizations coming together in this very transformative time, as you think about the role of an orchestrator inside an organization, it is really that simple. Your brand delivering the experience that your customers expect. Are we exceeding those expectations more often than not? And if the answers to those questions are, yes, maybe you've you've gotten the golden ticket. I think there's a lot of work to do for you and them to continue to get there. But what I'm really excited about is the clarity of vision and the opportunity that sits in front of us in a place where, as I've mentioned before, you know, you and them is not a brand everybody knows, but we are really focused on being the easiest part of a difficult moment. And it's not just sort of what we do with who we are as an organization and how we want to show up for our customers. Every single Polly. It's, it's just so inspiring. I, I, I have to say that the vision of where the company sees its brand going, how you translate that into customer experience. And you know, frankly, eventually how you create a flywheel because as you do more with customers and provide richer experiences, you get more data, you learn more about them, you use that to fuel the innovation and your ability to delight them and serve them better. And I just think the way you're thinking about it and mobilizing the organization to do so is an icon that many of us can learn from. I know I certainly have in this call, and I do in my conversations with you. So thank you very much. And in closing, I want to thank Pega for their sponsorship of this webinar series. It's been 3 so far. We have one more coming up where we really delve into the modern CMO mind, a mind that's dealing with a lot of different variables in the landscape, but also at a time of incredible opportunity, as Polly just cited, where it's not just about executing marketing. It's about leading strategy, bringing the customer to the center, mobilizing all of the information capabilities towards delivering customer value and seeing the outcome of that as the growing equity of your brand. I want to thank you all for listening. Please feel free to send any follow up questions. Polly and I are both on LinkedIn, actively on there and I look forward to seeing you at our next webinar. title: Apr 14, 2026 Taseko Updates Florence Copper and Gibraltar First Quarter Production
summary: Trekor Metals is a dynamic and growing mining company focused on the operation and development of mines in North America.
body_text: Taseko Updates Florence Copper and Gibraltar First Quarter Production View PDF version of this release: All 2026 News Releases April 14, 2026, Vancouver, BC – Taseko Mines Limited (TSX: TKO; NYSE American: TGB; LSE: TKO) (“Taseko” or the “Company”) is pleased to provide an operational update and first quarter production results for Florence Copper and the Gibraltar Mine. As previously announced, the Florence Copper SX/EW plant commenced operations in mid-February and first copper cathodes were harvested at the end of February. For the first quarter, a total of 1.5 million pounds of copper cathode was produced. Solutions have been flowing in the wellfield since late 2025 and initial copper leaching and production is in line with expectations, based on our modeling. The recent operational focus has been on balancing solution flow and grades from the wellfield through to cathode production. Stuart McDonald, President and CEO of Taseko, commented, “We are happy with the results from the first months of in-situ copper production at Florence. With the successful start-up behind us, the focus is turning to the production ramp-up. Additional newly constructed wells are now being integrated into the system, which will allow for higher solution flows and copper production in the coming weeks. Wellfield expansion continues, with four drills currently operating and a fifth expected to commence shortly.” Gibraltar produced a total of 30.0 million pounds of copper and 717 thousand pounds of molybdenum in the first quarter, a 50% and 113% increase over the same period in 2025. Copper grades in the quarter were in line with the life of mine average grade and recoveries improved to 83%. Copper sales in the first quarter were 27 million pounds, slightly lower than production due to shipment timing. “It was a solid quarter at Gibraltar and operating results were generally in line with our expectations. Production included 733 thousand pounds of copper cathode from the Gibraltar SX/EW plant which operated continuously through the winter months.” added Mr. McDonald. “Despite recent global events, copper markets have remained very strong and the average LME copper price in the first quarter was 16% higher than the previous quarter. Diesel prices have also increased and, at current levels, would increase Gibraltar operating costs by approximately US$0.10 to US$0.15 per pound this year. At Florence Copper, we have a fixed price contract in place for all sulphuric acid requirements in 2026, so do not expect any impact from recent inflationary pressure and global supply chain issues. Overall, we continue to anticipate strong financial performance from steady Gibraltar production and growing production from Florence Copper.” For further information on Taseko, see the Company’s website at tasekomines.com or contact: Investor enquiries Brian Bergot, Vice President, Investor Relations – 778-373-4554 Stuart McDonald President and CEO No regulatory authority has approved or disapproved of the information contained in this news release. title: Organize Your Study Materials to enhance your Learning
summary: Discover how Kaagaz simplifies your study routine by scanning and organizing student documents and notes digitally. Enhance clarity and accessibility with Kaagaz's innovative features. Try it today!
body_text: Benefits of Using a PDF Scanner for Students Efficient Note-taking and Organization Using a PDF scanner, students can quickly convert handwritten notes, textbook pages, or lecture slides into digital format. This not only saves time spent on rewriting but also ensures that all notes are neatly organized and easily accessible on devices like laptops, tablets, or smartphones. Organizing notes digitally allows for quick searching and referencing during study sessions. Convenient Study Material Compilation By scanning textbooks, articles, and other reference materials, students can create comprehensive digital study guides. These guides can include notes, highlighted sections, and annotations made directly on the scanned documents. This approach streamlines study preparation and revision, offering a consolidated resource that is portable and easy to navigate. Effortless Assignment Submission Instead of dealing with the hassle of printing and physically submitting assignments, students can scan completed work and submit it digitally. This method ensures clarity and legibility, avoids transportation issues, and allows for last-minute edits or corrections before submission deadlines. Digital submissions also make it easier for teachers to provide feedback electronically. Enhanced Collaboration and Sharing PDF scanners enable students to share scanned documents with classmates or teachers effortlessly. This feature facilitates collaborative projects, group study sessions, and peer review processes. By sharing digital copies, students can receive feedback, exchange ideas, and collectively work on assignments regardless of their physical locations. Environmental Responsibility and Cost Savings Opting for digital scans over printing reduces paper usage, contributing to environmental conservation efforts. It also helps students save on printing costs associated with producing multiple copies of study materials or assignments. Digital documents are durable and can be archived and accessed indefinitely without concerns about physical wear and tear. Platform: Web For: All users with connected Shopify stores AI Shot List: Professional product shots from a single photo ​ Getting multiple visuals per product doesn't have to mean multiple shoots. No manual photoshoot, no guessing what to shoot, just a complete set of images for every product in your catalog. Platform: web For: all users Learn more about Photoroom for Shopify More control for AI Shadows Users have full control over the position of the shadow. You can now specify if an object is laying flat or standing upright for the shadow to generate at the correct angle, allowing products to look more real and accurate. Platform: web app For: all users Learn more about AI Shadows API updates AI shadows with full control Generic AI shadows break catalog consistency. Teams processing thousands of product images need the same shadow direction, softness, and intensity across every SKU, not a different interpretation per image. AI shadows now supports full control over how the shadow looks. Set shadow.mode to ai.auto-with-overrides and use five override parameters to fix the appearance: shadow.softnessOverride for hard or soft edges, shadow.intensityOverride for how dark the shadow is, shadow.spreadOverride for shadow length ( short , medium , long ), shadow.directionOverride for direction relative to the subject (eight presets or degrees), and shadow.subjectPoseOverride for flat lay or upright subjects. Leave any override unset to let the model decide. Setting all five produces a fully deterministic shadow, which is what catalog teams need for consistent output at scale. This is a preview feature. Enable it by adding the HTTP header pr-ai-shadows-model-version: 2026-04-15 to your call. View examples and try it in the API here . Platform: now available via API. Also available on web, iOS, and Android. Video generator Static product images don't convert the way motion does. Teams that want product videos are stuck choosing between manual video editing, production agencies, or stitching together multiple tools per SKU. Video generator is now available via API through the /v1/animate endpoint. Upload an input image, specify animation parameters such as aspect ratio and mode, and the API returns a short animated product video. The endpoint supports free-form text prompts, so teams can cover custom scene or motion directions beyond pre-defined modes, and connect the API to their own LLM to dynamically generate prompts from image content and metadata. Built for food delivery catalogs, marketplace listings, and e‑commerce teams scaling to thousands of product videos. Available on the Enterprise plan. Multiple images to one video Single-image-to-video covers most product videos but not all. Categories like cars, furniture, and large consumer goods need 360-degree product spins, which require multiple input images stitched into a single coherent video. Marketplace and classifieds catalogs scaling thousands of listings can't do this with single-image inputs. The Video API now accepts up to 7 reference images alongside the main input on the /v1/animate endpoint. Pass them via referenceImages.<name>.imageFile (e.g. referenceImages.back.imageFile , referenceImages.detail.imageFile ) to drive a single coherent video from multiple angles. When references are used, generation is prompt-driven — pair them with a free-form prompt to direct the scene, motion, or hero shot. Built for marketplaces, classifieds, and e‑commerce teams generating 360-degree product spins and cinematic hero shots at scale. Async by design — submit the job, poll statusUrl , download from resultUrl when complete. View the full parameter reference and request access here . Edit with AI now accepts up to 4 additional reference images alongside the main input, for a total of 5 images per call. Set editWithAI.additionalImages to pass the extra references. The model can combine elements across the inputs in a single output, for example placing a product into a reference scene, transferring a style from one image to another, or pulling an object out of one image and into another. View the full parameter reference and try it in the API here . Platform: now available via API. title: 4 effective strategies for getting more done with ADHD
summary: Work with your ADHD – not against it – with these 4 tried and true strategies
body_text: Do you have ADHD and find it difficult to figure out which tasks to pick without getting anxious about making the right choice? Do you feel like you're always procrastinating? Is it normal for you to be doing a dozen tasks at once — but getting nothing done? These can make you feel frustrated and irritated with yourself. But being hard on yourself won't get things done. So we've compiled a list of 4 strategies for getting more done if you have ADHD. 4 Strategies For Getting Things Done When You Have ADHD Break down a big task into smaller tasks When you have ADHD, it can be difficult to focus on big tasks, as they seem overwhelming (even for people without ADHD!). Because of that, your brain shuts down, and makes you feel like you want to run and hide. How to-do lists feel like for non-ADHD vs. ADHD folks - Source So break a big task down into smaller tasks that you can imagine completing. If it is a time-sensitive project, estimate how long it will take you to do each small task and assign a 'planned' time to each one. Do keep some wiggle room with planned time because we generally underestimate the amount of time it takes to get things done. Set a really low bar just to get yourself started. So a tiny task can be “create a new document” or “choose a cover page for the presentation." This will make your to-do lists less overwhelming, and you will be able to focus on them without feeling anxious. Like the comic? Find more on @ sunsamahq on Instagram You can use tools like Sunsama to help you create a task list and jot down the subtasks you need to do to check off the main task. Crossing things off of the to-do list one by one will give you the motivation to move on to the next thing. Sunsama — an ADHD friendly daily planning assistant Work in short time bursts Managing ADHD in an age when we are constantly connected to the internet can feel impossible with all distractions at our fingertips. The trick is to schedule time for distractions and stay focused in short time bursts with the Pomodoro technique. Pomodoro is a time management technique where you do focused work for 25 minutes followed by a five-minute break. You can use online apps built to implement this technique and make it even simpler. Flow Club’s Lounge includes a Pomodoro timer, task list, and a curated focus playlist Using Pomodoro will also give you transition time between tasks — especially for the ones that put higher amounts of cognitive load. Take breaks longer than five minutes if you need more time to recharge. Use these breaks to take a walk, sip your favorite tea or meditate for a few minutes. Avoid doing things that will make your brain hyperactive (checking social media, chatting with colleagues, or worrying about things you have to do in the near and distant future) Set a time limit on your task (aka Timeboxing) People with ADHD are often perfectionists as they tend to overcompensate for symptoms they see as behavior flaws. That's why, sometimes, even with the Pomodoro technique, you can get stuck on a task. For example, you might keep working on a presentation deck for all the Pomodoros (25-min work slots) you have in the day. How do you avoid that from happening? The answer is — timeboxing, which is to allocate a fixed time period to a planned activity. And then you put that down in your calendar. It’s just like scheduling a meeting in your calendar. Once you block a time, treat it like a meeting. So no canceling, rescheduling, or distraction during that time period. This way, you can see how much time you've dedicated to the task and not go overboard. Here's an example: You have a presentation to work on that's due in two days. In your calendar, you block out six Pomodoros (2.5 hours) for that task on Tuesday afternoon. And then, on Wednesday, you can block one Pomodoro to review what you have and make any necessary changes. What if, even after organizing your list and setting the time limit for each task, you still don’t feel motivated to get started? Is there a way to address this obstacle? Let's find out in the next section. Join a virtual co-working space If procrastination is stopping you from getting work done, this strategy is for you. Find someone who needs to get work done as well, and work with them in real-time. They don't have to help you with your task or vice-versa. They can work on their tasks while you work on yours. It's called a coworking session. It works because coworking provides connection, accountability, & focus — the three things that can help you get work done on time. Opening up the virtual session, greeting your work partner(s), and checking in are signals that tell your brain that it's time to work on the task at hand and help you become less distracted. When you commit to someone that you will get your tasks done, you are more likely to stay focused to keep your promise. If you are interested in virtual coworking sessions, check out Flow Club . It's an online coworking community. The entire co-working process is guided by a host, so you never have to figure anything out to get all of the benefits. Make ADHD your superpower Living with ADHD can be frustrating at times. Before you give up for the day, try just a little harder by giving yourself that extra push with tools — be it guided daily planning with Sunsama or virtual co-working with Flow Club. It never hurts to try. Most people dealing with ADHD find that even basic planning and some automation sets them on their way to having a productive workday. However, while it's great to strategize and maximize your productivity, be aware of burnout as well — especially if you experience hyperfocus as a symptom of your diagnosis. Make sure you schedule downtime every day after a certain time and for at least one full day every week. Along with practicing the strategies mentioned above, carve out some time at the end of your day (10-15 min) and end of the week (1-1.5r) to reflect on how you managed your time & work. Don't just think about areas of improvement, but celebrate the wins as well. Those will tell you what worked so you can double down on those strategies. If you’re having trouble focusing, here’s some strategies for that are known to help neurodivergent folks focus and be productive. Read More: How to Focus With ADHD ADHD doesn’t need to be a struggle. It is often a superpower that fuels out-of-the-box thinking and creativity, keeps you full of energy, and enables you to really focus and thrive with deep work. ‍
